:
The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.16,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 01.05.2023.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 01.05.2023 at about 6.15 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Access Scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JA- 5185 near 6th Main, 100 feet Road, Indiranagar,
Bengaluru City, at that time, all of a sudden the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.
No.KA-11-A-6217 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the SCCH-10 petitioner's Motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
the injured petitioner was shifted to hospital and took inpatient treatment.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
The respondent No.1 being insurer and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the present petition.
3. In pursuance to the Petition notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Despite service of notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
4. The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle has contended that, the claim petition filed by the SCCH-10 petitioner is not maintainable.
The respondent No.1 had denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-A-6217.
Further, denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Shiva Kumar.

2 vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: Further contended that, the petitioner has filed the false case against the offending vehicle for wrongful loss to this respondent.

Further, the respondent No.1 has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age,
avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.1 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
SCCH-10

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-A-6217 by its driver, in RTA took place on 01.05.2023 at about 6.15 p.m., on 6th Main 100 Feet Road, Indira Nagar, Bengaluru ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, what amount and from whom ?
3 ) What order or award?

6. The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and also Medical Record Officer of Rajalakshmi Hospital as PW-2 and the doctor as PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21.
The respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

SCCH-10 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :
R E A S O N S 9. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.16,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 01.05.2023.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0088/2023 of Jeevan Bhima Nagar Shiva Kumar.V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163826423/
3 (Indiranagar) Traffic PS and the First information statement.

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.1, it reveals that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-A-6217 for the commission of offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Jeevan Bhima Nagar (Indiranagar) Traffic PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.7, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Rupesh. V, who is none other than the driver of the offending Goods Carrier Vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-A-6217 for the offence punishable under section SCCH-10 279 and 338 of IPC.
10.
Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.5 produced by petitioner and Ex.P.8 discharge summaries, it appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

11. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Goods Carrier vehicle showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records, it reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
12. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of SCCH-10 negligence is not required.

This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.
13.

entities.text:
Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-A-6217.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:-

The petitioner contended that, after the accident, he was shifted to Axon Speciality hospital, Bengaluru and after first aid and for further treatment he was shifted to Rajalakshmi hospital & Research Center, Bengaluru, wherein he took inpatient treatment and spent more than SCCH-10 Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.

15. Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.

sentences.text: Future Medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.5.

As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained Contusion with deformity of the left knee 7 cm x 5 cm and MRI shows - full thickness ACL tear, displaced fracture lateral femoral condyle and the doctor opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
16. In this case, the petitioner has produced three discharge card as per Ex.P.8 of Rajalakshmi hospital and SCCH-10 Research Center, Bengaluru.

On perusal of first discharge summary, it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital on 02.05.2023 and discharged on 05.05.2023,
on perusal of second discharge summary it reveals that the petitioner again admitted to said hospital on 01.06.2023 and discharged on 02.06.2023 and third discharge summary disclose that the petitioner again admitted the said hospital on 16.06.2023 and discharged on 22.06.2023.
17.
Ex.P.9 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.3,66,175/-, Ex.P.10 are the advance receipts and Ex.P.11 are the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills and same is rounded off to Rs.3,66,000/- under the head of Medical expenses.
18. As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might Shiva Kumar.

V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163826423/
5 have suffered pain and agony.

entities.text: V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: SCCH-10
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
19. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that due to the disability he has lost his earning capacity.

In order to establish the disability, the doctor was examined before the Court as PW-3.
PW-3 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained, a) Left knee ACL, PCL,
MCL, LCL tear, B) Medial Patellar retinaculum tear left knee, C) Bucket handle tear of medial meniscus left knee and d) Horizontal tear of medial meniscus left knee.
The petitioner was treated conservatively with above knee slab and discharged on 05.05.2023.

The petitioner was readmitted to said hospital on 01.06.2023 and he was treated conservatively and was discharged on 02.06.2023 and again SCCH-10 the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital on 16.06.2023 and the petitioner was operated with arthoroscopic CL + PCL reconstruction using hammstring and peroneus longus graft + lateral meniscal balancing and discharged on 22.06.2023.

Further, PW-3 deposed that he recently examined the petitioner on 14.10.2024 for assessment of disability and on examination it is found that healed surgical scar left knee with implant in situ, persistent instability of left knee, complains of pain and stiffness in left knee and ankle and complaints of difficulty in squatting, sitting on floor, climbing stairs and walking.
Further, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability for left lower limb is 38%.

20. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 47 years at the time of accident and he was doing Vegetable Business and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m. In order to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has SCCH-10 to be taken into consideration.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 01.05.2023.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,000/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
SCCH-10 21.
On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.

sentences.text: As per the doctor, the permanent physical disability for left lower limb is 38%.
It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 38% permanent disability to the left lower limb and he has not assessed the whole body disability, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 12%.
23. To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card and Driving licence as per Ex.P.14 and SCCH-10 Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15, the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 05.01.1977.
The accident was occurred on 01.05.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 46 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 13.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 12%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,92,000/-(Rs.16,000 x 12).

Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,92,000/-(annual income) X 13 (multiplier) X 12%
= Rs.2,99,520/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.2,99,520/-.
24.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability, he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.

Hence, I conclude that if Rs.30,000/-
is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.
SCCH-10 25

. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
1) Medical expenses Rs. 3,66,000 /-
2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 15,000 /-
 Loss of Future earning Rs. 2,99,520/-
4) capacity due to permanent  disability 5) Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,50,520/-.
26. REGARDING LIABILITY:

As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods Carrier vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-A-6217.
In this case, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.1, as such, respondent No.1 has to indemnify the SCCH-10 respondent No.2.

Shiva Kumar.V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163826423/
7

entities.text: Shiva Kumar.V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 insurer and the respondent No.2 owner are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.1 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation of Rs.7,50,520/- along with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,50,520/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
SCCH-10
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.

Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,50,520/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.1 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
